## Code Status

Merged on 2026-11-17 from Part A of `robustness_analyses.qmd` and sections 1, 2 and 6 of
`final_checks.qmd` (now in `scripts/archive/`). The code is unchanged. None of these
sections draws random numbers. Not yet rendered on the real data.

## Purpose

Checks that the tone and style findings generalize, plus two descriptive tables for the
capstone write-up.

1.  **Sample characteristics** (Table 5, Section 7.2).
2.  **Style gap by tone, in full**, with equivalence tests (Table 8, Section 7.4).
3.  **Messages as a random effect.** Each tone is represented by 24 specific messages.
    Do tone and style differences hold up when the messages are treated as a sample of
    possible messages, not as the tones themselves? (Section 7.11)
4.  **Message text and reading level.** Are tone differences explained by message
    length or other surface features? Which individual messages did best and worst?
    And what reading level did the messages reach, against the prompt's 8th-grade
    target? (Section 7.11)
5.  **Repetition within the session.** Do ratings fall as people work through the
    three rating blocks, and does any tone wear out faster? This is the only evidence
    in the panel on the variety premise. (Section 7.11)
6.  **Drinking severity.** Do the conclusions hold among respondents with higher AUDIT
    scores, who are closer to the population the system is for? (Section 7.11)

The stricter-exclusion check reported in Section 7.11 is in `methods_candidates.qmd`
(Section 12), because it summarises the method results computed there.

## Setup

```{r}
#| label: Setup
options(conflicts.policy = "depends.ok")
library(tidyverse)

source("https://github.com/jjcurtin/lab_support/blob/main/format_path.R?raw=true")
source(here::here("scripts", "functions_llmpanel.R"))
source(here::here("scripts", "functions_assignment.R"))

path_processed <- format_path("llmpanel/data_processed")
raw_panel <- read_csv(here::here(path_processed, "panel.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)

# tone_levels and pref_cols are defined in functions_llmpanel.R
tone_label <- \(x) str_to_sentence(str_replace_all(x, "_", " "))

set.seed(102030)
n_boot <- 1000

# Variables format_eda() drops: AUDIT score and the position (1-3) of each risk
# context's rating block
extras <- raw_panel |>
  select(subid, audit_score, block_order_hi, block_order_hd, block_order_li)

panel_long <- format_eda(raw_panel, long = TRUE) |>
  left_join(extras, by = "subid") |>
  mutate(
    position = case_when(context == "high_increasing" ~ block_order_hi,
                         context == "high_decreasing" ~ block_order_hd,
                         context == "low_increasing" ~ block_order_li),
    # One id per distinct message: 4 message sets x 3 contexts x 5 tones x 2 styles
    message_id = paste(survey_version, context, tone, style, sep = "|"),
    subid_f = factor(subid),
    tone_f = factor(tone, levels = tone_levels),
    style_f = factor(style),
    context_f = factor(context))

n_distinct(panel_long$subid)
n_distinct(panel_long$message_id)                       # expect 120
panel_long |> distinct(message_id, tone) |> count(tone) # expect 24 per tone
panel_long |> count(position)                           # expect 1, 2, 3 in equal numbers
```

# 1. Sample Characteristics

For Table 5 of the report. Race and ethnicity categories are not mutually
exclusive (check all that apply).

```{r}
#| label: Sample Table
n_total <- nrow(raw_panel)
n_total

# Continuous
raw_panel |>
  summarise(across(c(dem_age, audit_score, dem_n_household),
                   list(mean = \(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE), sd = \(x) sd(x, na.rm = TRUE),
                        min = \(x) min(x, na.rm = TRUE), max = \(x) max(x, na.rm = TRUE),
                        missing = \(x) sum(is.na(x))))) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = c("variable", ".value"),
               names_pattern = "(.*)_(mean|sd|min|max|missing)$") |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 2)))

# Categorical
count_levels <- function(v) {
  raw_panel |>
    count(level = as.character(.data[[v]])) |>
    mutate(variable = v, pct = round(100 * n / n_total, 1), .before = 1)
}
c("dem_sex", "dem_orientation", "dem_education", "dem_income", "dem_marital_status",
  "dem_student", "dem_minority") |>
  map(count_levels) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  relocate(variable, level, n, pct) |>
  print(n = Inf)

# Race and ethnicity (each is "selected" when not missing)
raw_panel |>
  summarise(across(starts_with("dem_race_"), \(x) sum(!is.na(x)))) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "category", values_to = "n") |>
  mutate(pct = round(100 * n / n_total, 1))

# White only vs. any other selection (the coding used in the analyses)
panel_long |> distinct(subid, dem_ethnicity) |> count(dem_ethnicity) |>
  mutate(pct = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1))

# AUDIT zones
raw_panel |>
  count(audit_zone = cut(audit_score, c(-Inf, 15, 19, Inf), labels = c("8-15", "16-19", "20+"))) |>
  mutate(pct = round(100 * n / n_total, 1))

# Collection window
range(raw_panel$start_date, na.rm = TRUE)
median(raw_panel$q_total_duration, na.rm = TRUE) / 60   # median minutes to complete
```

# 2. Style Gap by Tone, in Full

For each tone, the gap is each respondent's mean informal rating minus their
mean formal rating. Each gap gets a paired t-test against zero and an
equivalence test (two one-sided tests) against a margin of 0.25 points. Holm
adjustment is across the six rows, separately for the difference tests and
the equivalence tests.

```{r}
#| label: Style Gap Table
equiv_margin <- 0.25

gap_by_tone <- panel_long |>
  summarise(rating = mean(rating_num, na.rm = TRUE), .by = c(subid, tone, style)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = style, values_from = rating) |>
  mutate(gap = informal - formal) |>
  select(subid, tone, gap)

gap_overall <- panel_long |>
  summarise(rating = mean(rating_num, na.rm = TRUE), .by = c(subid, style)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = style, values_from = rating) |>
  transmute(subid, tone = "all tones", gap = informal - formal)

bind_rows(gap_by_tone, gap_overall) |>
  drop_na(gap) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_gap = mean(gap),
    ci_low = t.test(gap)$conf.int[1],
    ci_high = t.test(gap)$conf.int[2],
    dz = mean(gap) / sd(gap),
    p = t.test(gap)$p.value,
    p_tost = max(t.test(gap, mu = -equiv_margin, alternative = "greater")$p.value,
                 t.test(gap, mu = equiv_margin, alternative = "less")$p.value),
    .by = tone) |>
  mutate(p_holm = p.adjust(p, "holm"),
         p_tost_holm = p.adjust(p_tost, "holm"),
         conclusion = case_when(p_tost_holm < .05 ~ "Equivalent to zero within the margin",
                                p_holm < .05 ~ "Different from zero, not shown equivalent",
                                .default = "Inconclusive")) |>
  arrange(desc(mean_gap)) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) signif(x, 3))) |>
  print(width = Inf)
```

A gap can be both different from zero and equivalent within the margin: that
means it is real but smaller than 0.25 points.

# 3. Messages as a Random Effect

Every analysis so far treats the 24 messages written in a tone as if they
were the tone. If a few messages happened to be unusually good or bad, a
"tone effect" could be a message effect. Adding a random intercept for
message asks whether tone and style differences are larger than the variation
between messages of the same kind. This is the stricter test, and the one
that supports claims about tones in general.

```{r}
#| label: Message Random Effect
m_people <- lme4::lmer(
  rating_num ~ tone_f * style_f + context_f + (1 | subid_f) + (1 | subid_f:tone_f),
  data = panel_long, REML = FALSE)
m_msg <- update(m_people, . ~ . + (1 | message_id))

# Is there variation between messages beyond tone, style and context?
anova(m_people, m_msg)
lme4::VarCorr(m_msg)
```

```{r}
#| label: Tone Tests With Messages Random
m_msg_no_int <- lme4::lmer(
  rating_num ~ tone_f + style_f + context_f +
    (1 | subid_f) + (1 | subid_f:tone_f) + (1 | message_id),
  data = panel_long, REML = FALSE)
m_msg_no_tone <- update(m_msg_no_int, . ~ . - tone_f)
m_msg_no_style <- update(m_msg_no_int, . ~ . - style_f)

# Tone, style, and tone-by-style, each tested against message variation
anova(m_msg_no_tone, m_msg_no_int)
anova(m_msg_no_style, m_msg_no_int)
anova(m_msg_no_int, m_msg)
```

```{r}
#| label: Tone Contrasts With Messages Random
emm_msg <- emmeans::emmeans(m_msg, ~ tone_f, lmer.df = "asymptotic")
emm_people <- emmeans::emmeans(m_people, ~ tone_f, lmer.df = "asymptotic")

# Same means, wider standard errors once messages are random
full_join(as_tibble(emm_people) |> select(tone_f, mean = emmean, se_people_only = SE),
          as_tibble(emm_msg) |> select(tone_f, se_messages_random = SE),
          by = "tone_f") |>
  mutate(se_ratio = se_messages_random / se_people_only) |>
  arrange(desc(mean))

pairs(emm_msg, adjust = "holm")
pairs(emmeans::emmeans(m_msg, ~ style_f, lmer.df = "asymptotic"))
```

Reading the results:

-   If the tone test is still significant and the top-two vs. bottom-two
    contrasts survive, the tone ranking can be claimed for tones in general.
-   If contrasts that were significant before are no longer, report the
    ranking as a property of these messages and say so in the limitations.
-   The message SD in `VarCorr` shows how much two messages of the same tone,
    style and context typically differ. Compare it with the spread of tone
    means (about 0.45 from top to bottom).

# 4. Message Text and Reading Level

Two separate looks at the message text: surface features against ratings (from
`robustness_analyses.qmd`), and an estimate of reading level against the prompt's
8th-grade target (from `final_checks.qmd`). An earlier pilot comparing several
grade-level formulas on the temperature-prompting messages is in
`scripts/archive/readability.qmd`.

## Surface features

Uses the message files in the repository
(`qualtrics_panel/output/prod_messages/version2/survey1` to `survey4`).
**Check that these are the fielded messages and that `survey1`-`survey4`
correspond to message sets `x1`-`x4`** before relying on this section. It is
skipped if the files are not found.

```{r}
#| label: Message Files
message_paths <- here::here("qualtrics_panel", "output", "prod_messages", "version2",
                            paste0("survey", 1:4), "production_messages.csv")
have_messages <- all(file.exists(message_paths))
have_messages
```

```{r}
#| label: Message Text
#| eval: !expr have_messages
messages <- map2(1:4, message_paths, \(v, p) {
  read_csv(p, show_col_types = FALSE) |> mutate(survey_version = paste0("x", v))
}) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  transmute(
    survey_version,
    context = paste(lapse_risk, lapse_risk_change, sep = "_"),
    style = formality,
    tone = case_when(message_category == "Legitimizing" ~ "legitimizing",
                     message_category == "SelfEfficacy" ~ "self_efficacy",
                     message_category == "Acknowledging" ~ "acknowledging",
                     message_category == "ValueAffirmation" ~ "value_affirmation",
                     message_category == "Norms" ~ "norms"),
    message_id = paste(survey_version, context, tone, style, sep = "|"),
    text = generated_message,
    n_words = str_count(text, "\\S+"),
    n_sentences = pmax(str_count(text, "[.!?]+(\\s|$)"), 1),
    words_per_sentence = n_words / n_sentences,
    letters_per_word = str_count(text, "[A-Za-z]") / n_words,
    you_per_100 = 100 * str_count(str_to_lower(text), "\\byou(r|rs|rself)?\\b") / n_words)

# Every rated message should match exactly one message file row
stopifnot(nrow(messages) == 120, !anyDuplicated(messages$message_id),
          setequal(messages$message_id, unique(panel_long$message_id)))

message_stats <- panel_long |>
  summarise(mean_rating = mean(rating_num), sd_rating = sd(rating_num), n_raters = n(),
            .by = message_id) |>
  inner_join(messages, by = "message_id")
```

*Text features by tone and style*

```{r}
#| label: Text Features
#| eval: !expr have_messages
message_stats |>
  summarise(messages = n(),
            across(c(mean_rating, n_words, words_per_sentence, letters_per_word, you_per_100),
                   mean),
            .by = tone) |>
  arrange(desc(mean_rating)) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 2)))

message_stats |>
  summarise(messages = n(),
            across(c(mean_rating, n_words, words_per_sentence, letters_per_word, you_per_100),
                   mean),
            .by = style) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 2)))
```

*Do surface features explain the tone and style effects?*

A message-level regression (120 messages). If tone and style coefficients
barely move when text features are added, length and wording density are not
what drives the ratings.

```{r}
#| label: Text Regression
#| eval: !expr have_messages
msg_data <- message_stats |>
  mutate(tone = factor(tone, levels = tone_levels), style = factor(style),
         context = factor(context))

lm_base <- lm(mean_rating ~ tone + style + context, data = msg_data)
lm_text <- update(lm_base, . ~ . + n_words + words_per_sentence + letters_per_word + you_per_100)

anova(lm_base, lm_text)
bind_rows(base = broom::tidy(lm_base), with_text = broom::tidy(lm_text), .id = "model") |>
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") |>
  select(model, term, estimate) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = model, values_from = estimate) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 3)))
summary(lm_text)$coefficients |> round(3)
```

```{r}
#| label: Text Plot
#| eval: !expr have_messages
# Each message's mean rating against its word count, with one overall trend line
message_stats |>
  ggplot(aes(x = n_words, y = mean_rating, color = tone, shape = style)) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  geom_smooth(aes(group = 1), method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "grey40") +
  scale_color_discrete(labels = tone_label) +
  labs(x = "Words in message", y = "Mean rating of the message", color = "Tone", shape = "Style")
```

*Best- and worst-rated individual messages*

Useful for the paper's examples, and for spotting a message that is carrying
(or sinking) its tone.

```{r}
#| label: Best and Worst Messages
#| eval: !expr have_messages
ranked <- message_stats |>
  arrange(desc(mean_rating)) |>
  transmute(rank = row_number(), mean_rating = round(mean_rating, 2), n_raters,
            tone, style, context, text)
ranked |> slice_head(n = 6) |> knitr::kable()
ranked |> slice_tail(n = 6) |> knitr::kable()

# Spread of message means within each tone-by-style cell (12 messages each)
message_stats |>
  summarise(lowest = min(mean_rating), highest = max(mean_rating),
            range = highest - lowest, .by = c(tone, style)) |>
  arrange(desc(range)) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 2)))
```

## Reading level

The prompt asked for an 8th-grade reading level. This estimates the
Flesch-Kincaid grade of each message. Syllables are counted with a simple
rule (vowel groups, minus a silent final "e"), so treat the grades as
approximate: good for comparing tones and styles, less so as absolute values.

Uses the message files found in the surface-features section above, and is skipped
if they are missing.

```{r}
#| label: Reading Level
#| eval: !expr have_messages
count_syllables <- function(word) {
  word <- str_to_lower(str_remove_all(word, "[^A-Za-z]"))
  if (nchar(word) == 0) return(0)
  n_syl <- str_count(word, "[aeiouy]+")
  if (str_detect(word, "[^aeiouyl]e$") && n_syl > 1) n_syl <- n_syl - 1
  max(n_syl, 1)
}

reading <- map(message_paths, \(p) read_csv(p, show_col_types = FALSE)) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  transmute(
    style = formality, tone = message_category, text = generated_message,
    n_words = str_count(text, "\\S+"),
    n_sentences = pmax(str_count(text, "[.!?]+(\\s|$)"), 1),
    n_syllables = map_dbl(str_split(text, "\\s+"), \(ws) sum(map_dbl(ws, count_syllables))),
    fk_grade = 0.39 * n_words / n_sentences + 11.8 * n_syllables / n_words - 15.59)

reading |>
  summarise(messages = n(), sentences = mean(n_sentences), words = mean(n_words),
            fk_min = min(fk_grade), fk_max = max(fk_grade), fk_mean = mean(fk_grade)) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 1)))

reading |>
  summarise(messages = n(), sentences = mean(n_sentences), fk_grade = mean(fk_grade),
            .by = style) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 1)))

reading |>
  summarise(messages = n(), fk_grade = mean(fk_grade), .by = c(tone, style)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = style, values_from = fk_grade) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 1)))

# Did every message keep to 3-4 sentences, as the prompt asked?
reading |> count(n_sentences)
```

# 5. Repetition Within the Session

The case for rotating tones assumes a tone wears out when repeated. The panel
cannot test months of daily use, but each respondent rated three blocks of ten
messages, and every block contains every tone twice. If ratings fall from the
first block to the third, or fall faster for some tones, that is a small,
within-session signal of wear. If nothing moves, the panel is silent on the
premise, which is also worth stating.

Block position was randomized across the three risk contexts, so position is
not confounded with context.

```{r}
#| label: Position Descriptives
position_summary <- panel_long |>
  summarise(mean_rating = mean(rating_num), sd_rating = sd(rating_num),
            .by = c(subid, position)) |>
  summarise(n = n(), mean = mean(mean_rating), se = sd(mean_rating) / sqrt(n()),
            within_person_sd = mean(sd_rating, na.rm = TRUE),
            .by = position) |>
  arrange(position)
position_summary

panel_long |>
  summarise(rating = mean(rating_num), .by = c(position, tone)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = position, values_from = rating, names_prefix = "block_") |>
  mutate(change_1_to_3 = block_3 - block_1) |>
  arrange(change_1_to_3)
```

```{r}
#| label: Position Models
pos_data <- panel_long |> mutate(position_f = factor(position))

m_pos0 <- lme4::lmer(
  rating_num ~ tone_f * style_f + context_f + (1 | subid_f) + (1 | subid_f:tone_f),
  data = pos_data, REML = FALSE)
m_pos1 <- update(m_pos0, . ~ . + position_f)
m_pos2 <- update(m_pos1, . ~ . + position_f:tone_f)

# Overall drift across blocks
anova(m_pos0, m_pos1)
emmeans::emmeans(m_pos1, pairwise ~ position_f, adjust = "holm", lmer.df = "asymptotic")

# Does the drift differ by tone? (a tone wearing out faster)
anova(m_pos1, m_pos2)
emmeans::emmeans(m_pos2, ~ position_f | tone_f, lmer.df = "asymptotic") |>
  emmeans::contrast("poly") |>
  as_tibble() |>
  filter(contrast == "linear") |>
  mutate(p_holm = p.adjust(p.value, "holm")) |>
  select(tone_f, linear_trend = estimate, SE, p.value, p_holm)
```

```{r}
#| label: Position Plot
# Mean rating of each tone in each rating block (in the order shown), with 95% intervals
panel_long |>
  summarise(rating = mean(rating_num), .by = c(subid, position, tone)) |>
  summarise(mean = mean(rating), se = sd(rating) / sqrt(n()), .by = c(position, tone)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = position, y = mean, color = tone, group = tone)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = mean - 1.96 * se, ymax = mean + 1.96 * se),
                  position = position_dodge(width = 0.15)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:3) +
  scale_color_discrete(labels = tone_label) +
  labs(x = "Rating block (order shown)", y = "Mean message rating", color = "Tone")
```

*Time spent per block*

Faster pages later in the session would suggest declining attention, which
would complicate reading a drop in ratings as wear.

```{r}
#| label: Position Timing
block_time <- raw_panel |>
  select(subid, matches("^x[1-4]_(hi|hd|li)_timing_page_submit$"),
         block_order_hi, block_order_hd, block_order_li) |>
  pivot_longer(matches("timing_page_submit$"), names_to = "block", values_to = "seconds") |>
  drop_na(seconds) |>
  mutate(ctx = str_extract(block, "(?<=_)(hi|hd|li)(?=_)"),
         position = case_when(ctx == "hi" ~ block_order_hi,
                              ctx == "hd" ~ block_order_hd,
                              ctx == "li" ~ block_order_li))

block_time |>
  summarise(n = n(), median_seconds = median(seconds), mean_seconds = mean(seconds),
            .by = position) |>
  arrange(position)

friedman.test(seconds ~ position | subid,
              data = block_time |> filter(n() == 3, .by = subid))
```

# 6. Drinking Severity

Respondents screened in at AUDIT 8 or higher and role-played recovery. Those
with higher scores are closer to the people the system is built for. If tone
and style results look the same across severity, the role-play limitation is
less worrying. Groups follow the standard AUDIT zones: 8-15 (hazardous), 16-19
(harmful), 20 or more (possible dependence).

```{r}
#| label: AUDIT Groups
audit <- raw_panel |>
  transmute(subid, audit_score,
            audit_group = cut(audit_score, breaks = c(-Inf, 15, 19, Inf),
                              labels = c("8-15", "16-19", "20+")))
audit |> count(audit_group) |> mutate(pct = n / sum(n))
summary(audit$audit_score)

rating_by_tone <- panel_long |>
  summarise(rating = mean(rating_num), .by = c(subid, tone)) |>
  left_join(audit, by = "subid")
rating_by_style <- panel_long |>
  summarise(rating = mean(rating_num), .by = c(subid, style)) |>
  left_join(audit, by = "subid")
```

```{r}
#| label: AUDIT Tone and Style
# Mean rating by tone within each severity group
rating_by_tone |>
  summarise(mean = mean(rating), .by = c(audit_group, tone)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = audit_group, values_from = mean) |>
  arrange(desc(`8-15`)) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 2)))

# Does the tone effect differ by severity? (audit_group:tone)
afex::aov_ez(id = "subid", dv = "rating",
             data = rating_by_tone |> mutate(subid = factor(subid)),
             within = "tone", between = "audit_group",
             anova_table = list(correction = "GG", es = "pes"))

# Does the informal advantage differ by severity? (audit_group:style)
rating_by_style |>
  summarise(mean = mean(rating), .by = c(audit_group, style)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = style, values_from = mean) |>
  mutate(informal_minus_formal = informal - formal)
afex::aov_ez(id = "subid", dv = "rating",
             data = rating_by_style |> mutate(subid = factor(subid)),
             within = "style", between = "audit_group",
             anova_table = list(es = "pes"))
```

```{r}
#| label: AUDIT Continuous
# Same questions with AUDIT as a continuous score (no arbitrary cut points)
m_audit0 <- lme4::lmer(
  rating_num ~ tone_f * style_f + context_f + audit_c +
    (1 | subid_f) + (1 | subid_f:tone_f),
  data = panel_long |> mutate(audit_c = audit_score - mean(audit_score)),
  REML = FALSE)
m_audit_tone <- update(m_audit0, . ~ . + audit_c:tone_f)
m_audit_style <- update(m_audit0, . ~ . + audit_c:style_f)
anova(m_audit0, m_audit_tone)
anova(m_audit0, m_audit_style)
# Do heavier drinkers rate messages higher or lower overall?
summary(m_audit0)$coefficients["audit_c", ]
```

The recommended method's gain by AUDIT group is in `methods_candidates.qmd`
(Section 9, Fairness), with the other group comparisons.
